prompt: Victory screen for an ink-and-wash world-conquest board game: the whole war shown as one finished ink painting. Full world map on deep indigo paper as in the reference, but now nearly every territory is soaked in a single winner's pigment (muted sage green), and layered over the map are the traces of the entire game: dozens of faint, overlapping dry-brush attack strokes in each player's muted color (vermilion, slate, ochre, sage) crossing borders, older strokes paler and more faded, newer ones darker, like a time-lapse of the war painted as a single calligraphic record. A thin hairline gold rule with a small gold ring sits near the bottom with, beneath it in an elegant serif, the only text: "Sage wins · 14 rounds". Quiet, archival, beautiful enough to frame. No kanji, no seals, no blossoms, no Fuji, no poems, no other text, no buttons.
